app_info.subtitle: Track labs in your own cloud
app_info.description: Health by Dr Brad keeps your health record as a single file in your own Dropbox or Google Drive. ChatGPT can read it, add measurements and lab results, correct a value entered wrongly, file the results from a lab report dropped into the chat, and compute a plan: what screening is due, and evidence-based suggestions with the citation behind each one. Your record and your own cloud credential are never stored on our servers, and no value is ever deleted; a correction appends the new number and marks the old row entered-in-error.

justifications.read_only_justification: Fetches the user's own record file, filters it and returns rows without writing anything back.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the calling user's own file in that user's own Dropbox or Google Drive, over that user's own credential.
justifications.destructive_justification: Writes nothing, so no value can be lost.

justifications.read_only_justification: Computes what is due and which suggestions apply from the record held in memory and returns them, adding or changing no row.
justifications.open_world_justification: Computes from the calling user's own file and our own evidence tables, and reaches nothing else.
justifications.destructive_justification: Modifies no row: it is a computation over a record it only reads.

justifications.read_only_justification: Appends one measurement row and writes the file back to the user's own cloud.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only to the calling user's own file, over that user's own credential.
justifications.destructive_justification: Appends only: no row is deleted or overwritten, and a second value on a day that already holds one is refused.

justifications.read_only_justification: Appends up to 50 lab rows in one call and writes the file back to the user's own cloud.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only to the calling user's own file, over that user's own credential.
justifications.destructive_justification: Append-only and all rows or none: existing rows are never deleted, and a duplicate test on the same day is refused.

justifications.read_only_justification: Appends the corrected row, flips the row it supersedes and writes the file back.
justifications.open_world_justification: Touches only the calling user's own file in that user's own cloud.
justifications.destructive_justification: It deletes nothing, but the superseded row is marked entered-in-error permanently, guarded by a required expected value and a 90-day age limit.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes sex, birth year, birth month or height into the record's profile and saves the file.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only to the calling user's own file, over that user's own credential.
justifications.destructive_justification: The profile is last-writer-wins, so a change overwrites what stood there; each changed field requires the value the caller expects to find, and a mismatch writes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Files a public GitHub issue on the project's repository for the user.
justifications.open_world_justification: It posts to GitHub's API on our own repository, carrying only what the assistant wrote about the problem; anything that reads as a health value, an email address, a phone number, a file name or a link carrying a token is refused before it is sent.
justifications.destructive_justification: It creates an issue and takes nothing away; the health record is neither read nor changed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Its extract phase parks candidate values in the user's own folder and its commit phase appends values and files documents.
justifications.open_world_justification: It sends a file from the user's own connected Dropbox folder, never the record, to Anthropic's API for extraction, and keeps nothing after extraction.
justifications.destructive_justification: A replace in commit marks the superseded row entered-in-error permanently, guarded by the expected value, a 90-day age limit and the user’s own confirmation.

justifications.read_only_justification: Appends the lab values the user confirmed and files the document as a metadata-only row in the user's own file.
justifications.open_world_justification: ChatGPT read the attached file, so the call carries only the values it read and reaches nothing outside the user’s own record.
justifications.destructive_justification: A replace flips the superseded row to entered-in-error permanently, guarded by the expected value, a 90-day age limit and the user’s own confirmation.

test_cases.description: Read the connected record, the first thing after sign-in.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the profile (male, born 1979, 178 cm), at least fifteen measurements and at least five lab results, among them a ferritin result, plus sections for medications, supplements, screenings and documents. Earlier reviewers may have added rows; that is expected. Nothing is written.

test_cases.description: Add one measurement the user states in the chat, on a past date.
test_cases.user_prompt: Record my weight on 2 March 2026 as 78 kg.
test_cases.expected_output: Appends one weight row dated 2 March 2026 and confirms the metric, value and date. If an earlier reviewer already recorded a weight on that date, the tool refuses a second value for the day and offers a correction instead: one value per test per day, never a silent overwrite. Either answer is correct.

test_cases.description: Compute the plan from the record.
test_cases.user_prompt: What should I do next about my health?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns current values, what screening is due, and evidence-based suggestions with a reason and citation each, in hedged educational wording. Nothing is written.

test_cases.description: File the results from a lab report dropped into the chat. ChatGPT reads the file itself; it never reaches our server.
test_cases.user_prompt: Here is my blood test. Add the results to my record. (Attach the synthetic lab PDF supplied with this submission, not a real person’s report.)
test_cases.expected_output: The first call writes nothing and returns each printed result matched against the record, with units and collection date, plus a receipt. After the user confirms in their own words, a second call commits: values appended, document filed as a metadata-only row. If an earlier reviewer already filed the same file, the first call says it was already imported and offers nothing to commit; that is correct too.

test_cases.description: Correct a value entered wrongly. The record is append-only, so the old row is superseded rather than edited.
test_cases.user_prompt: My most recent ferritin should be 10 ug/L higher than it shows.
test_cases.expected_output: Reads the record for the most recent ferritin row, its id and its current value, then returns a confirm receipt naming that value and the value 10 ug/L higher, and writes nothing. After the user’s own yes, a second call appends a ferritin row with the higher value at the original date and marks the old row entered-in-error. Nothing is deleted and nothing is invented.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for a general medical question that does not touch the user's own record.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What does high ferritin usually mean?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked. ChatGPT answers from its own knowledge.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for diet planning. The app stores and reads a health record and writes no meal plans.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Write me a seven-day meal plan for lowering my cholesterol.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because the request is outside its supported workflows.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for booking or contacting a clinician. The app has no scheduling, directory or messaging.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Book me an appointment with a doctor near me this week.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it cannot book or contact anyone.
